title: The decision is not the enforcement
question: When one authorization input changes, which component changes the decision and where must a deny stop the action?
scenario: Dr. Reyes is signed in through SSO on a managed tablet during her scheduled shift. She requests a sensitive patient record. Her role permits clinical reads, but the current care-team assignment is the fact that determines whether this patient is in scope.
focalRelation: The PDP evaluates current subject, object, action, and context attributes; the API PEP enforces the scoped result before the record operation.

nodes.label: Dr. Reyes
nodes.detail: Authenticated clinician; authentication identifies the subject but does not authorize this record read.

nodes.label: Read request
nodes.detail: Subject: Reyes; object: patient 1842; action: read; device: managed; shift: active; care team: current value.

nodes.label: Policy decision point
nodes.detail: Evaluates current attributes and policy version; returns permit, deny, or a defined step-up obligation.

nodes.label: Record API enforcement
nodes.detail: Mediates the resource operation and applies the PDP result even if the UI or token would otherwise allow a request.

nodes.label: Patient record
nodes.detail: The protected object. No denied path reaches this node.

nodes.label: Decision evidence
nodes.detail: Records subject, object, action, policy, context, result, obligation, and enforcement outcome for review.

edges.label: permits read only when result is current

states.title: Freeze the complete request
states.caption: All decision inputs are visible before prediction; a valid sign-in is only one input.

states.title: Evaluate current context
states.caption: The PDP receives the care-team assignment along with role, object, action, device, and shift.

states.title: Return a scoped permit
states.caption: The assigned relationship produces a permit for this patient, this read action, and this request context.

states.title: Enforce before the record
states.caption: The API PEP applies the permit and only then allows the record operation.

states.title: Change one attribute
states.caption: The same token, role, device, shift, patient, and action remain; only care-team assignment changes to none.

states.title: Deny stops at enforcement
states.caption: The PDP returns deny; the API PEP blocks the operation before the record and records the outcome.

variants.label: Stale permit, missing device context
variants.changedFact: A cached permit exists, but current device-compliance evidence is missing and policy requires it for this read.

states.title: Detect stale evidence
states.caption: The PEP sees that the prior result lacks required current device context.

states.title: Request a fresh result
states.caption: The PEP sends current inputs to the PDP rather than inferring compliance from the old permit.

states.title: Hold the boundary
states.caption: Access remains stopped until policy-defined evidence or step-up produces a new scoped result.

nodes.label: Authenticated clinician
nodes.detail: The requester has a valid identity, but authentication alone does not settle this authorization.

nodes.label: Read request without device evidence
nodes.detail: The current request lacks device compliance required by policy.

nodes.label: Fresh policy evaluation
nodes.detail: The decision point evaluates current identity, relationship, action, and device evidence.

nodes.label: API enforcement point
nodes.detail: The enforcement point rejects the cached permit and requests a current result.

nodes.label: Protected patient record
nodes.detail: The record is not reached unless a new scoped permit or defined step-up succeeds.

nodes.label: Authorization decision record
nodes.detail: Evidence records the stale permit rejection and enforced outcome.

edges.label: permits access only on fresh result

prediction.prompt: Only the care-team assignment changes from assigned to none. What should change the outcome, and where must the deny take effect?

options.label: The PDP reevaluates current context; the API PEP blocks the read
options.feedback: Correct. The PDP computes the scoped result and the PEP enforces it at the protected operation.

options.label: The valid sign-in token keeps the read permitted.
options.feedback: Authentication identifies Dr. Reyes. It does not override the changed patient relationship used by authorization.

options.label: Hide the record in the UI; the API may still return it.
options.feedback: UI hiding is not resource mediation. The API PEP must stop the operation before the record.

options.label: The PDP directly blocks the database read.
options.feedback: The PDP returns a decision. The PEP mediates and blocks the resource operation.

prediction.hint: Name the component that computes a result separately from the component placed on the resource path.

transfer.prompt: A cached permit exists, but required current device-compliance context is missing. What is the defensible next action?

options.label: Reuse the permit because the token has not expired.
options.feedback: Token lifetime does not prove authorization context is current. Reject or bypass the stale result.

options.label: Obtain a fresh result and apply deny or the defined step-up before access
options.feedback: Correct. The changed issue is evidence freshness, so the PEP must obtain and enforce a current policy result.

options.label: Treat missing compliance as compliant until the next review.
options.feedback: Missing required evidence cannot silently become a favorable attribute.

transfer.hint: Ask whether the prior result contains every attribute the current policy requires.

retry.prompt: A broad administrator role grants one engineer both payment creation and approval. Which change repairs the authorization design?

options.label: Require a longer password while leaving the conflicting permissions unchanged.
options.feedback: Authentication strength does not remove the incompatible permission combination.

options.label: Hide the approval button for normal users.
options.feedback: A hidden button does not prevent direct API use. The authorization boundary must mediate the action.

options.label: Separate the actions into incompatible roles and enforce both at their APIs
options.feedback: Correct. Separation of duties constrains the permission combination, and each protected action still needs enforcement.

retry.hint: Focus on the incompatible actions and the points that actually execute them.

takeaway: Authentication names the subject; authorization evaluates a current, scoped request; enforcement must stop an unauthorized operation at the resource boundary.
assumptions: The example policy requires a current care-team assignment for ordinary access.
A defined break-glass path would be a separate conditional result with its own logging and review.
Animation timing, if used by the renderer, represents presentation pacing rather than system latency.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: Implemented in 6 stable decision states: Dr. Reyes submits authenticated request Read request; Read request supplies current decision inputs Policy decision point. The model keeps Dr. Reyes, Read request, Policy decision point, Record API enforcement, Patient record, Decision evidence distinct. Its changed case is “A cached permit exists, but current device-compliance evidence is missing and policy requires it for this read.” and every option returns to a named repair state.
